page: Amazon Web Services c8g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Utilizing the arm64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 391.61 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 171.76 GB/sec. The Geekbench multi-core score of 21709.0 and Passmark database operations score of 46834.4 also place this instance in the top tier. Strong performance is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with clang, and static web serving throughput, which reaches 72.97 GB/sec. However, performance is average for stress-ng CPU tests and weak for prompt processing on large 70B LLM models, which registers at 5.89 tokens/sec.

The c8g.8xlarge offers high resource density for compute-bound tasks without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. Its qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the ARMv9 architecture, which delivers strong memory bandwidth and database operations relative to its hardware class. This profile makes the instance suitable for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression. It is less suited for large-scale LLM prompt processing due to architectural limitations in large-model inference.

Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of memory, and a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or GPU. Benchmarks show top-tier memory bandwidth, with uncached read-only speeds of 391.61 GB/sec, and strong database operation performance. While it achieves top-tier Geekbench multi-core scores and strong software compilation speeds, it exhibits average performance in standard CPU stress tests and weak performance in large-model LLM prompt processing. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads, making it highly suitable for database operations, web serving, and software compilation tasks that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth.
